subject: POC Integration: Lumen Retail trial — technical handoff & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sara Liu <sara@lumenretail.com>
Cc: Alex Martinez <alex.m@lumenretail.com>
Date: 2028-03-01T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Discovery — POC next steps

Hi Sara / Alex,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on the user flows and where Redwood can help reduce latency & costs on your inference layer. Per our discussion, attaching a concise POC outline (POC-outline.pdf) that captures what we talked through. Quick recap and asks so we can lock the trial: 

Summary (from today's discovery)
- Primary goal: reduce average response latency for product recommendation synthesis and keep token cost under target to justify model selection.
- Target workload: ~5k daily requests initial, peak bursts to 50 RPS for cart-time personalization.
- Data sensitivity: PII in product titles only; overall compliance requirements captured in the attached doc.

Proposed POC scope (high level)
1) Integration: Redwood SDK (Python/Node) + streaming route for real-time carts.
2) Success criteria: latency P99 < 500ms (end-to-end), avg token cost < $0.006 per API call, and >= 90% match to golden responses on the 250-test prompt set.
3) Duration: 4 weeks (2-week integration + 2-week evaluation).
4) Owners: Lumen Eng lead (Alex) to provide sandbox creds & sample payloads; Redwood SE (we'll assign) to deliver SDK sample, route config, and instrumentation hooks.

Key asks for you: please confirm the success criteria above and provide a list of 3 prioritized evaluation prompts and a sandbox endpoint we can hit by 3/6. If you have an internal SLA target that differs, flag it.

Technical notes we plan to propose to your team:
- Use Redwood streaming endpoint (/v1/stream/generate) for cart-level responses to keep perceived latency low.
- Configure prefix/KV caching for the product catalog prompts to save tokens on repeated context.
- Suggested model variants: rwd-small-quant (fast/quantized) for baseline cost run and rwd-medium for a quality comparison.

I'll loop in our Solutions team next for a technical handoff. Can you confirm a preferred time for the kickoff (we recommend 30–45 min) this week or early next?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Marissa / team,

Draft integration plan & execution timeline below. Kept it tight so we can iterate before the kickoff on 3/7. Attaching an integration sketch (integration-sketch.png) to the Drive link in the thread.

High-level technical approach
- Primary path: Redwood streaming endpoint (/v1/stream/generate) for cart-time personalization. Secondary path: synchronous generate (/v1/generate) for batch scoring.
- SDKs: provide Python (redwood==0.9.x) and Node (redwood-js@0.6.x) examples. Both include helper wrappers for function/tool calling and streaming consumption.
- Model routing: default to rwd-small-quant for latency baseline, can fall back to rwd-medium for quality checks. We will use runtime routing policy to prefer fastest region and fallback to rwd-medium in case of mismatches.

Integration milestones (dates, owners)
1) 2028-03-03 (Karthik) — Deliver integration sketch & short tech-deck.
2) 2028-03-04 (Aditya) — Provide SDK examples and a sample script that hits: 
   - POST /v1/generate (sync) — body: {"model":"rwd-small-quant","input":<prompt>}
   - POST /v1/stream/generate (streaming) — server-sent events with chunked tokens; example includes function-calls as JSON payloads on-the-fly.
3) 2028-03-05 (Ben) — Security brief: KMS integration details, sample audit log retention policy, and SOC 2 evidence pointer.
4) 2028-03-07 (All) — Kickoff call; run a live integration demo and smoke test with their sandbox host.
5) 2028-03-21 — End of 4-week POC evaluation window; compare metrics vs success criteria.

Technical details & considerations
- Streaming details: recommend chunk size tuned to 32–64 token windows to balance latency and throughput. Use SSE with an initial metadata frame including request_id and route_hint.
- KV caching: identify product catalog prefix; we expect 30–40% token savings for repeat catalog prompts. Include cache TTL of 1h for POC.
- Batching: continuous batching will be enabled on the Redwood runtime; advise initial max batch wait 5ms to keep P99 low.
- Token accounting: instrument per-route token breakdown (prompt / completion / cache savings) and publish to telemetry endpoint for CS.
- Function/tool-calling: provide example where the model returns a function call: {"name":"getProductInfo","arguments":{...}} and Redwood will post the call to the configured tool endpoint (we'll include the sample tool adapter). For streaming, function-calls will be emitted as a final JSON chunk once resolved.
- Fallback policy: on elevated latency or token budget exceed, route to rwd-small-quant or a trimmed prompt template; include automatic alert to CS at 2x token target.

Deliverables attached (links in Drive):
- integration-sketch.png (diagram of SDK -> Streaming -> Tool Adapter -> Telemetry)
- sample-scripts: python_stream_example.py, node_stream_example.js (to be attached to the kickoff Drive folder)
- telemetry checklist: per-route traces, token breakdown, anomaly alerting thresholds.

Open questions for Lumen (to confirm before kickoff)
- Sandbox host and sample payload shape (Alex to provide by 3/6).
- Any rate limits or IP allow-listing we should pre-configure for the sandbox.
- Preferred retention window for audit logs (we'll draft a recommended policy but need their target).

If this looks good I'll finalize the deck and post the Drive folder with the sample scripts before EOD 3/03.

Thanks,
